newsitem.title: USA: Ross Stores January sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Ross Stores January sales rise.

text.p: Ross Stores Inc Thursday said sales for the four weeks ended February 1, totaled $96 million, a 25 percent increase from the $77 million in sales for the four weeks ended February 3, 1996, and comparable store sales for the month rose 15 percent.

For the 13 weeks ended February 1, sales totaled $510 million, a 22 percent increase above the $418 million in sales for the 13 weeks ended February 3, 1996. Comparable store sales for the quarter rose 14 percent.

For the 52 weeks ended February 1, sales totaled $1.69 billion, a 20 percent increase above the $1.41 billion in sales for the 52 weeks ended February 3, 1996. Comparable store sales for the 52 weeks rose 13 percent.

"Business in January outperformed our expectations, continuing the strong momentum we have experienced throughout the past year," said Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Balmuth. "The solid double-digit growth in same-store sales this month is especially encouraging in light of the tough comparison we faced in January 1996 when same store sales were up 10 percent."
"This trend makes us optimistic about our ability to continue to show respectable sales and earnings gains in 1997," he said.
